protocol.description:
Some desktops show minimized ("iconic") windows as icons, on the desktop or in a panel. This protocol lets a client learn where the icon of its toplevel is shown, draw that icon itself with an ordinary wl_surface, and mark the toplevel as an iconlet: a program whose icon is its user interface, such as a clock, a battery gauge or a load meter, and whose window is never meant to be shown.
The icon's position is meant for drawing things that relate to the rest of the screen, such as eyes following the pointer with the help of ext-image-copy-capture-v1's cursor sessions. A compositor may hide this global from clients it doesn't trust with it.
This is an experimental protocol: backward-incompatible changes may be made, and the interface names carry the "xx" prefix until it is stabilized.

interface.name: xx_iconlet_manager_v1
interface.description: The global object for creating xx_iconic_toplevel_v1 objects.

entry.name: already_constructed
entry.summary: the toplevel already has an xx_iconic_toplevel_v1 object

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the manager. Objects created with it are unaffected.

request.name: get_iconic_toplevel

description.summary: extend a toplevel with icon state

request.description:
Create an xx_iconic_toplevel_v1 object for the toplevel. Creating a second one for the same toplevel while the first exists raises the already_constructed error.
It may be created at any time, but a client that means to call set_iconlet should do so before the toplevel's initial commit, so that it is never shown.

interface.name: xx_iconic_toplevel_v1
interface.description:
Tells where the icon of a toplevel is shown while it is minimized, and lets the client draw that icon and declare the toplevel an iconlet.
If the xdg_toplevel is destroyed first, this object becomes inert: it gets no more events and its requests are ignored.

entry.name: icon_surface_exists
entry.summary: the toplevel already has an icon surface

entry.name: role
entry.summary: the wl_surface already has another role

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the object. The toplevel stops being an iconlet if it was one; whether it is then shown is up to the compositor. An icon surface created from this object stays alive but is no longer shown.

request.name: set_iconlet
request.description:
Declare the toplevel an iconlet: a program whose icon and title are its whole user interface. Unlike most surface state this applies right away, not with the next commit.
The compositor should then keep the toplevel minimized from the start and never show it, also not when the user activates its icon (it sends the activate event instead) and not when a taskbar or an xdg_activation_v1 token asks for it. It should leave the toplevel out of window lists, window switchers and focus cycling, and should give its icon a prominent and stable place, ahead of the icons of other minimized windows, so that it doesn't move when those come and go.
The toplevel still needs a buffer to be mapped; a single pixel will do.

request.name: get_icon_surface

description.summary: draw the icon with a surface

request.description:
Give the wl_surface the xx_icon_surface_v1 role: while the toplevel is minimized, the compositor shows the surface's content as the toplevel's icon, in place of the one set with xdg-toplevel-icon-v1 or picked by the compositor. Until the surface has a buffer, the compositor shows its usual icon.
The surface works like any other: buffers can be changed at any time and are not required to stay unchanged, frame callbacks pace updates, and wl_surface.preferred_buffer_scale, fractional scaling and viewporter apply. Subsurfaces may be added. It gets no input events: the compositor keeps handling clicks on the icon. Frame callbacks are only sent while the icon is shown.
Raises icon_surface_exists if the toplevel already has an icon surface, and role if the wl_surface has a role other than xx_icon_surface_v1.

event.name: icon_geometry
event.description:
The toplevel's icon is shown, or moved, to the given rectangle on an output, in logical coordinates relative to the output's top-left corner. The rectangle is the icon image, not including a label the compositor may show with it.
The output is null if the client has no wl_output object for it.
This event is sent whenever the rectangle changes; icon_hidden ends it.

event.name: icon_hidden

description.summary: the icon is no longer shown

event.description: The toplevel's icon is no longer shown, for example because the toplevel was restored. Sent only after icon_geometry.

event.name: activate

description.summary: the user activated an iconlet's icon

event.description:
The user activated the icon of an iconlet, for example by double-clicking it. The compositor didn't show the toplevel; the client may respond by opening another window.
The token is an xdg_activation_v1 token that lets such a window take focus. It may be empty if the compositor doesn't offer one.
Only sent after set_iconlet.

interface.name: xx_icon_surface_v1

description.summary: a surface drawing a toplevel's icon

interface.description: The role object of an icon surface, see xx_iconic_toplevel_v1.get_icon_surface.

request.name: destroy
request.description: The surface is no longer shown as the icon; the compositor shows its usual one again. The wl_surface keeps the role and may only be used again for another xx_icon_surface_v1.

event.name: configure
event.description: The size of the icon in logical pixels. It is sent once the role is assigned and whenever it changes. Content of another size is scaled or cropped by the compositor.
